messages:
noah: Heads up — spotted 3 preemptible GPU nodes get reclaimed in us-west1 during a canary deploy. Several pods with local PVs ended up in Terminating state, blocked by `local-storage` mounts. CA trimmed cluster down right after the reclaim.
maya: Ugh. Do we have the scale-down timings too aggressive? Which CA flags are we running now?
jia: We defaulted to: --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m, --scale-down-delay-after-add=2m, --expander=least-waste. (from the helm chart)
riya: 10m unneeded time sounds low for GPUs + local volumes. Also check --skip-nodes-with-local-storage is enabled? If not CA will try to evict pods on nodes with local PVs which can hang.
sam: It was disabled (we wanted to reclaim empty GPU machines faster). But maybe that backfired when preemptible nodes come back mid-schedule.
noah: Timeline: node preempted at 10:12, new spot node came up at 10:15, CA considered old node unneeded and marked for deletion at 10:20, then stuck draining because of a sidecar writing to a hostPath. Blocker lasted ~18m and pushed several jobs to queue.
maya: For immediate mitigation, can we bump --scale-down-unneeded-time to 30m and enable --skip-nodes-with-local-storage? Also set --max-empty-bulk-delete=1 so we don't nuke multiple nodes at once.
jia: I agree. Proposed flags patch: 
```
--scale-down-unneeded-time=30m 
--scale-down-delay-after-add=10m 
--max-empty-bulk-delete=1 
--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=true 
--expander=most-pods 
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
```
riya: Suggest keeping expander=least-waste for cost but add --scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5 to avoid evicting partly used GPUs. Also consider --ignore-daemonsets-utilization=true if not set.
sam: We also need to audit pod spec: any pods using hostPath or local PV should have proper PDBs or tolerations, and annotate to opt-out of CA evictions e.g., topology.kubernetes.io/prevent-scale-down=true (internal convention).
noah: Ops-bot: can you run a dry-run diff on the CA helm values against staging with the proposed flags? (cc @ops-bot)
ops-bot: running helm diff for chart cluster-autoscaler (release=cluster-autoscaler-staging)...
ops-bot: diff found: +--scale-down-unneeded-time=30m, +--max-empty-bulk-delete=1, +--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=true, +--scale-down-delay-after-add=10m, +--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5
ops-bot: no breaking API changes. Would apply in 1 min if approved.
maya: Approve. Let's stage to canary cluster first (apply to staging us-west1) and monitor pod term counts, drain durations, and queuing latency.
noah: Also add an alert: CA node drain duration > 5m with pods in Terminating -> fire a page to eng-oncall, we had silent impact.
riya: I'll open a short runbook update: how to identify local-PV blocked drains, commands to force delete safely, and our annotation to prevent scale-down. Link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/ca-gpu-drain
sam: Long-term: consider nodegroup separation for preemptible GPUs vs reserved GPUs and set different scale policies. Preemptible groups can be less aggressive with scale-down, reserved ones can be tighter.
jia: Agreed. Also evaluate using a CA expander plugin that respects GPU packing (avoid leaving one GPU node half-used). We should run sim tests with our job mix.
maya: I'll handle the helm rollout to staging (10:40) and post metrics in #eng-infra. If staging looks good we can roll to prod tomorrow morning with maintenance window.
noah: Thanks. Also add a small note for dev teams: ensure jobs that write to hostPath use terminationGracePeriodSeconds and post-stop hooks to flush. Otherwise they block node removal.
riya: Marking follow-ups: 1) patch CA flags in helm repo, 2) run sim for expander behavior, 3) update runbook, 4) create alert. I'll track in the infra board.
noah: Great. If anything else pops up tag me. :thumbsup:
